arxiv-2103-16762.title: Weakly-Supervised Image Semantic Segmentation Using Graph Convolutional Networks
arxiv-2103-16762.description: Abstract This work addresses weakly-supervised image semantic segmentation based on image-level class labels. One common approach to this task is to propagate the activation scores of Class Activation Maps (CAMs) using a random-walk mechanism in order to arrive at complete pseudo labels for training a semantic segmentation network in a fully-supervised manner.

arxiv-2311-09273.title: In-vehicle Sensing and Data Analysis for Older Drivers with Mild Cognitive Impairment * Corresponding Author Thanks: This research was supported by the U.S. National Institute of Health (NIH) (R01 AG068472 02S1) and National Science Foundation (NSF) (OAC 1948066). PubID: pubid: ©2023 IEEE. Personal
arxiv-2311-09273.creator: 1 st Sonia Moshfeghi, 2 nd Muhammad Tanveer Jan, 3 rd Joshua Conniff, 4 th Seyedeh Gol Ara Ghoreishi, 5 th * Jinwoo Jang, 6 th Borko Furht, 7 th Kwangsoo Yang, 8 th Monica Rosselli, 9 th David Newman, 10 th Ruth Tappen, 11 st Dana Smith
arxiv-2311-09273.description: Abstract Driving is a complex daily activity indicating age and disease-related cognitive declines. Therefore, deficits in driving performance compared with ones without mild cognitive impairment (MCI) can reflect changes in cognitive functioning. There is increasing evidence that unobtrusive monitoring of older adults’ driving performance in a daily-life setting may allow us to detect subtle early changes in cognition.

arxiv-2408-11530.title: Scalable Knowledge Refactoring using Constrained Optimisation
arxiv-2408-11530.creator: Minghao Liu, David M. Cerna, Filipe Gouveia, Andrew Cropper
arxiv-2408-11530.description: Abstract Knowledge refactoring compresses a logic program by introducing new rules. Current approaches struggle to scale to large programs. To overcome this limitation, we introduce a constrained optimisation refactoring approach. Our first key idea is to encode the problem with decision variables based on literals rather than rules. Our second key idea is to focus on linear invented rules.

arxiv-2410-03714.title: Perceptual Analysis of Groups of Virtual Humans Animated using Interactive Platforms
arxiv-2410-03714.creator: Rubens Montanha, Giovana Raupp, Ana Carolina Schmitt, Gabriel Schneider, Victor Araujo, Soraia Raupp Musse
arxiv-2410-03714.description: Abstract Virtual humans (VH) have been used in Computer Graphics (CG) for many years, and perception studies have been applied to understand how people perceive them. Some studies have already examined how realism impacts the comfort of viewers. In some cases, the user’s comfort is related to human identification.

arxiv-2502-02559.title: A Family-Based Approach to Safety Cases for Controlled Airspaces in Small Uncrewed Aerial Systems
arxiv-2502-02559.creator: Michael C. Hunter, Usman Gohar, Myra B. Cohen, Robyn. R. Lutz, Jane Cleland-Huang
arxiv-2502-02559.description: Abstract As small Uncrewed Aircraft Systems (sUAS) increasingly operate in the national airspace, safety concerns arise due to a corresponding rise in reported airspace violations and incidents, highlighting the need for a safe mechanism for sUAS entry control to manage the potential overload.

arxiv-2506-17580.title: Context-Aware Scientific Knowledge Extraction on Linked Open Data using Large Language Models PubID: pubid: 0000–0000/00$00.00 © 2021 IEEE
arxiv-2506-17580.creator: Sajratul Yakin Rubaiat, Hasan M Jamil
arxiv-2506-17580.description: Abstract The exponential growth of scientific literature presents a significant challenge for researchers seeking to extract and synthesize relevant knowledge. Traditional search engines often return a large number of sources without directly providing detailed answers, while general-purpose Large Language Models (LLMs) may offer concise responses that lack depth or fail to incorporate the most up-to-date information.

arxiv-2509-08499.title: Heart Disease Prediction: A Comparative Study of Optimizers’ Performance in Deep Neural Networks This work was done while Author 1 was a research intern at SAIL Innovation Lab, supervised by Author 2.
arxiv-2509-08499.creator: Chisom Chibuike, Adeyinka Ogunsanya
arxiv-2509-08499.description: Abstract Optimization has been an important factor and topic of interest in training deep learning models, yet less attention has been given to how we select the optimizers we use to train these models. Hence, there is need to dive deeper into how we select the optimizers we use for training and the metrics that determine this selection.

europmc-pmc7323511.creator: Okba NMA, Müller MA, Li W, Wang C, GeurtsvanKessel CH, Corman VM, Lamers MM, Sikkema RS, de Bruin E, Chandler FD, Yazdanpanah Y, Le Hingrat Q, Descamps D, Houhou-Fidouh N, Reusken CBEM, Bosch BJ, Drosten C, Koopmans MPG, Haagmans BL.

Although molecular diagnostic tests were rapidly developed, serologic assays are still lacking, yet urgently needed. Validated serologic assays are...

pmc-10575401.title: Recent Advancements and Strategies for Overcoming the Blood–Brain Barrier Using Albumin-Based Drug Delivery Systems to Treat Brain Cancer, with a Focus on Glioblastoma
pmc-10575401.creator: Camelia-Elena Tincu (Iurciuc), Călin Vasile Andrițoiu, Marcel Popa, Lăcrămioara Ochiuz
pmc-10575401.description: Glioblastoma multiforme (GBM) is a highly aggressive malignant tumor, and the most prevalent primary malignant tumor affecting the brain and central nervous system. Recent research indicates that the genetic profile of GBM makes it resistant to drugs and radiation. However, the main obstacle in treating GBM is transporting drugs through the blood–brain barrier (BBB).

pmc-10643265.title: Correlation between the density of defect states (DDS) and cross-linking of corner/edge sharing GeSe4 tetrahedral structural units
pmc-10643265.creator: Shiv Kumar Pal, A Dahshan, Neeraj Mehta
pmc-10643265.description: We have estimated the DDS in the STSG [Se78-xTe20Sn2Gex (x = 0, 2, 4, 6)] system by using the Correlated Barrier Hopping (CBH) model by performing A.C. conduction measurements in the frequency range (1 kHz–10 kHz) and temperature underneath the glass transition temperature (303–333) K. The detailed analysis reveals that bi-polaron hopping is a leading conduction mechanism over single-polaron hopping.

pmc-11295717.title: Automation of duplicate record detection for systematic reviews: Deduplicator
pmc-11295717.creator: Connor Forbes, Hannah Greenwood, Matt Carter, Justin Clark
pmc-11295717.description: BackgroundTo describe the algorithm and investigate the efficacy of a novel systematic review automation tool “the Deduplicator” to remove duplicate records from a multi-database systematic review search.MethodsWe constructed and tested the efficacy of the Deduplicator tool by using 10 previous Cochrane systematic review search results to compare the Deduplicator’s ‘balanced’ algorithm to a semi-manual EndNote method.

pmc-11380455.title: Integrative alternative splicing analysis reveals new prognosis signature in B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia
pmc-11380455.creator: Zhiyi Zhuo, Junfei Wang, Yonglei Zhang, Guoyu Meng
pmc-11380455.description: The dysregulation of alternative splicing (AS) is increasingly recognized as a pivotal player in the pathogenesis, progression, and treatment resistance of B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (B-ALL). Despite its significance, the clinical implications of AS events in B-ALL remain largely unexplored.

pmc-11496707.title: Silicon-based double fano resonances photonic integrated gas sensor
pmc-11496707.creator: Norhan A. Salama, Shaimaa M. Alexeree, Salah S. A. Obayya, Mohamed A. Swillam
pmc-11496707.description: The telecommunication wavelengths are crucial for developing a photonic integrated circuit (PIC). The absorption fingerprints of many gases lie within these spectral ranges, offering the potential to create a miniaturized gas sensor for PIC. This work presents novel double Fano resonances within the telecommunication band, based on silicon metasurfaces for selective gas sensing applications.

pmc-11510571.title: Advances in Neuroprotection in Glaucoma: Pharmacological Strategies and Emerging Technologies
pmc-11510571.creator: Li-Hsin Wang, Chun-Hao Huang, I-Chan Lin
pmc-11510571.description: Glaucoma is a major global health concern and the leading cause of irreversible blindness worldwide, characterized by the progressive degeneration of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and their axons. This review focuses on the need for neuroprotective strategies in glaucoma management, addressing the limitations of current treatments that primarily target intraocular pressure (IOP) reduction.

pmc-11526431.title: Extracellular Vesicle Mobility in Collagen I Hydrogels Is Influenced by Matrix-Binding Integrins
pmc-11526431.creator: Nicky W Tam, Alexander Becker, Agustín Mangiarotti, Amaia Cipitria, Rumiana Dimova
pmc-11526431.description: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are a diverse population of membrane structures produced and released by cells into the extracellular space for the intercellular trafficking of cargo molecules. They are implicated in various biological processes, including angiogenesis, immunomodulation, and cancer cell signaling.

pmc-11830927.title: IL-6–174 G/C transversion might decrease male infertility risk: A case-control study
pmc-11830927.creator: Tayyebeh Zamani-Badi, Mohammad Karimian, Javad Amini Mahabadi, Atieh Rafatmanesh, Hossein Nikzad
pmc-11830927.description: BackgroundGenetic predispositions have been identified as important factors in male infertility. Among the many genes related to male reproductive function, interleukin 6 (IL-6) has emerged as a key player. Despite the growing recognition of genetic factors in male infertility, the specific association between the IL-6–174 G/C genetic polymorphism and male infertility remains an area that needs further investigation.

pmc-12495613.title: Trends and dynamics of homelessness in Hong Kong: evidence from population survey in 2015 and 2021
pmc-12495613.creator: Siu Ming Chan, Hung Wong, Yikang Chen, Shennan Li, Ka-Ki Chung, Ying Crystal Chan
pmc-12495613.description: This study examines trends in homelessness in Hong Kong, comparing data from surveys conducted in 2015 and 2021. The research aims to identify trends and contributing factors, explore context-specific factors, analyze the relationship between housing, employment, and homelessness, and determine factors influencing its duration. Data from the H.O.P.E.

pmc-12595830.title: Therapeatic evaluation and single cell analysis of adipose stromal vascular fraction isolation from a commercial cell separation system
pmc-12595830.creator: Shunxin Han, Qian Zhang, Feng Lu, Junrong Cai
pmc-12595830.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundIn the field of regenerative therapy, the stromal vascular fraction (SVF) extracted from adipose tissue has been widely recognized for its significant benefits. However, the cellular composition and therapeutic effect of SVF products prepared via different methods are unclear.MethodsSVF cells were obtained via three approaches: (1) generation of the SVF via mechanical emulsification (M-SVF), (2) generation of the SVF via laboratory enzymatic digestion (L-SVF), and (3) generation of the SVF via commercial cell separation systems (C-SVF).

pmc-12827469.title: An innovative technique and laboratory protocol for CO2 storage in water disposal wells and monitoring asphaltene deposition
pmc-12827469.creator: Ehsan Jafarbeigi, Shahab Ayatollahi
pmc-12827469.description: Injecting CO2 into water-disposal wells is a promising strategy for geological carbon storage. However, this process can destabilize asphaltenes in residual oil blobs—primarily of the emulsified type – trapped within trapped in the porous rock, leading to precipitation that threatens storage integrity and operational safety.

pmc-13230804.title: Forecasting toxic metal concentrations in an inland sea ecosystem with machine learning algorithms
pmc-13230804.creator: Aylin Ucan, Nihat Tak, Asli Hocaoglu-Ozyigit, Ibrahim Ilker Ozyigit
pmc-13230804.description: In recent years, statistical and data-driven modeling approaches have been increasingly employed to predict element concentrations and to examine relationships among environmental features. In this context, the integration of feature selection techniques with machine learning models enhances model generalization and reduces model complexity by enabling the identification of key elements that are strongly associated with the target feature.

pmc-13280267.title: The State of the Art in Chronic Prurigo Nodularis
pmc-13280267.creator: Esther Serra-Baldrich, Ángeles Flórez, Marc Julià Manresa, Francisco Javier Ortiz de Frutos, José-Juan Pereyra-Rodriguez, Bibiana Pérez, Ignasi Figueras
pmc-13280267.description: Chronic prurigo nodularis (CPN) is a highly burdensome chronic inflammatory dermatosis characterized by intensely pruritic papulonodular lesions that may persist for years. Its pathophysiology reflects a neuro–immune–fibrotic axis in which type-2 cytokines (IL-4/IL-13/IL-31), neuropeptides, and profibrotic signaling interact to sustain the itch–scratch cycle and dermal fibrosis.

pmc-13422009.title: Genomic and Epidemiological Characterization of DENV‐1 and DENV‐2 Co‐Circulation During the 2023–2024 Dengue Epidemic in Espírito Santo, Brazil
pmc-13422009.creator: Nicolli Ribeiro de Jesus, Caio Santos de Souza, Mariene R. Amorim, João Paulo Cola, Raquel Gomes Catozo, Bruno Luiz M. Guedes, Bruna Caetano Pimenta, Julia Sthefany Nunes Zordan, Yasmim Barcellos Madeira Rosa, Henrique Tamanini Silva Moschen, Aline Souza Areias, Tatiane Comerio, Isabela Valim Sarmento, Julia Miranda Fardin, Daniel Claudio de Oliviera Gomes, Kiven Kumar, Eng Eong Ooi, Camila Malta Romano, Creuza Rachel Vicente

pmc-13655399.title: Atopic Dermatitis and Sleep Disorders
pmc-13655399.creator: Genlong Bai, Xinyi Shao, Yi Ou, Jin Chen, Zhaofu Tan, Aijun Chen, Jingbo Zhang
pmc-13655399.description: PurposeAtopic dermatitis (AD) is a common inflammatory skin disease affecting 129 million people worldwide and is characterized by recurrent eczema, severe pruritus, and skin barrier damage. Previous studies on AD-sleep disorder associations were limited by small sample sizes or single-center designs, lacking large-scale epidemiological evidence.
